name: NEPAL
lead: Nepal sits between India and China. Eight of the world's ten tallest mountains are here. Rhinos roam its steamy jungles. Snow leopards prowl its icy peaks. The Buddha, a great teacher, was born here too.
geo: Nepal stretches 800 km from east to west. It has four climate zones. The south is flat and steamy. The north has eight peaks above 8,000 m.
Nepal has no sea, but thousands of rivers run from melting snow. The Kali Gandaki Gorge drops over 5,500 m between two peaks.
animals: Rhinos and Bengal tigers live in Chitwan National Park. River dolphins swim in the jungle rivers. Wild elephants wade through tall grass.
Shy snow leopards hunt high among the glaciers. Red pandas nap in flowering forests. The Danphe, or Himalayan monal pheasant, is the national bird.
culture: Nepal is Hindu and Buddhist at once. Temples to Shiva, a Hindu god, stand beside golden stupas (Buddhist shrines). Dashain and Tihar (festival of lights) fill streets with colour and marigolds.
The Newari people built Kathmandu Valley's stacked-roof temples over 1,000 years ago. Sherpas guide climbers up the mountains. People say Namaste with hands pressed together.
history: The Buddha was born in Lumbini around 563 BCE. Rival kingdoms ruled the valleys for centuries. King Prithvi Narayan Shah joined them into one Nepal in 1768.
Nepal was the last Hindu kingdom until 2008, when people voted to have no king. Gurkha soldiers from Nepal fought beside British forces.
wows: Nepal's flag is the world's only national flag that is not a rectangle.
Everest, the highest mountain above sea level, rises 8,849 m.
Lumbini, where the Buddha was born, is a holy place to visit.
Nepal has 124 languages, more than most countries ten times bigger.
The Kali Gandaki Gorge is deeper than America's Grand Canyon.
Legend says a god drained Kathmandu Valley's lake with one sword stroke.
Mountain guide Kami Rita Sherpa has climbed Everest 32 times, a world record.

myths.myth: Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth
myths.fact: Measured from base to peak, Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller. Most of it hides under the sea.

myths.myth: Yetis are real animals in the Himalayas
myths.fact: DNA tests on hair and bones said to be from yetis showed they came from bears.
